result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers name the truncated axis as the main problem, suggest the same fixes (start at zero or switch to a line chart, add value labels, use an honest title), treat the 3D effect and bright green as secondary, and present the 2.7% rise as steady but modest. A includes a muddled claim that the 'visual gap is almost 3× the real one,' which doesn't match its own correct 7.5× figure. B's numbers are consistent (about 94% vs 12% of the visible height, roughly 8x), and it explains clearly why a line chart can use a zoomed axis honestly while a bar chart can't. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers identify the cut-off axis as the main problem, recommend a zero baseline or a labeled line chart, add values, retitle honestly and treat the 3D effect as secondary. B gives the more precise 7.5× figure, but then says the visual gap is 'almost 3× the real one,' which is wrong and confusing: the bars look 7.5 times as tall for a 2.7% difference. A's numbers are consistent throughout, and it clearly explains why a line can use a zoomed axis honestly while bars can't.
